summary.intent: Execute Phase 65 of the GSD workflow for cipher-box, implementing SDK write-chain, bin re-link, and invite-claim features across 7 plans in 4 waves using parallel git worktree execution. The user also requested that /ship-phase be launched after all waves complete.

workflow: Post-merge typecheck gate catches cross-plan consumer surface mismatches that per-plan builds miss — per-plan agents run vitest + targeted tsc, which can pass even when strict project typecheck fails due to unchecked consumers
Fixer agent pattern: when a gate fails, delegate to a focused foreground agent with an objective bar (typecheck exit 0 + tests green + committed) rather than fixing inline in the orchestrator context
Wave 1 manifest records worktree metadata (path, branch, base SHA) as plans complete, enabling ordered merge sequencing after all workers finish
Bash pipe through tail can silently consume exit codes; use explicit exit code capture (e.g., PIPESTATUS or separate exit capture) for gate commands
Full monorepo test suite is RAM-heavy — run sequentially per affected package rather than concurrently from parallel subagents
Single-plan waves (Waves 3–4) skip worktree overhead and run on the main tree; multi-plan waves use worktrees only when plans have no file overlap

friction: 65-04 plan under-scoped files_modified to only shared-write.ts, but SharedWriteContext reshape broke context.ts, client.ts, types.ts, and the web projection hook — post-merge typecheck caught it but required a separate fix agent and added significant latency
Bash pipe through tail ate the typecheck exit code on the first Wave 2 gate run, requiring a re-run with explicit exit capture

65-02 (bin re-link) required 131 tool uses and ~45 minutes — significantly heavier than the other Wave 1 plans (65-01: 32 tool uses, 65-03: 40 tool uses), suggesting the bin re-link model was more ambiguous than planned
The fixer agent also had to bridge apps/web (not in 65-04's plan scope at all), extending the blast radius of the scope gap
